claim: PIE's DE AUPRC is 1.2-3.2x the strongest baseline in each generalization setting
quote: For predicting differentially expressed genes, PIE achieves 1.2–3.2 times the AUPRC of the strongest baseline in each setting

claim: PIE learns population-level effects per condition because this gives a more direct training signal and aids generalization
quote: PIE focuses on learning population-level effects for each condition. This provides a more direct training signal for perturbation effects and facilitates generalization to new conditions.

claim: Representing each output gene by its description and evidence lets PIE predict seen and unseen genes
quote: Because each output gene is represented using its description and available experimental evidence, PIE can predict outcomes for both seen and unseen genes during training.

claim: Same-pert and Same-context Evidence are randomly zeroed in training so the model learns to predict without them
quote: During training, we randomly set Same-pert and Same-context Evidence to zero for a subset of samples, so that the model learns to predict when either channel is unavailable, as it is for unseen perturbations and contexts.

claim: Main benchmark Replogle–Nadig has single-gene CRISPRi knockdowns in K562, RPE1, HepG2 and Jurkat
quote: comprising single-gene knockdowns in four cell lines (K562, RPE1, HepG2, and Jurkat)

claim: Cross-dataset training excludes all cell lines shared with the held-out dataset, including derived lines
quote: We exclude from training all cell lines shared with the held-out dataset, including derived cell lines, so this experiment requires generalization to both an unseen dataset and unseen contexts.

claim: Unseen contexts: PIE AUPRC 0.424 vs Rhaister-O 0.344
quote: For unseen contexts, its AUPRC is 0.424, compared with 0.344 for Rhaister-O, the strongest baseline

claim: Unseen contexts: Rhaister-O beats PIE only on Spearman effect size (0.741 vs 0.734)
quote: The exception is Spearman effect size, where Rhaister-O scores 0.741 and PIE scores 0.734.

claim: Unseen perturbations: PIE AUPRC 0.304 vs TabICL 0.094, >3-fold
quote: For unseen perturbations, PIE has an AUPRC of 0.304 versus 0.094 for TabICL, a greater than threefold improvement.

claim: With both entities unseen, context mean is the only applicable model and PIE beats it on every metric
quote: When both entities are unseen, PIE exceeds context mean, the only applicable model, on every metric

claim: Both unseen: PIE Discrimination Score L1 0.643 vs context mean 0.502 (effectively random)
quote: reaching an AUPRC of 0.239 versus 0.088 and a Discrimination Score L1 of 0.643 versus 0.502 (effectively random)

claim: PIE also significantly beats the strongest baseline on Jiang et al. and Tahoe-100M within-dataset
quote: PIE significantly outperforms the strongest baseline on several metrics including AUPRC in similar experiments conducted on Jiang et al. and Tahoe-100M.

claim: Cross-dataset, seen perturbations: PIE AUPRC 0.378 vs Rhaister-O 0.283
quote: Its AUPRC is 0.378 versus 0.283 for Rhaister-O, the strongest baseline

claim: Cross-dataset, seen perturbations: perturbation mean beats PIE on DE direction match (0.733 vs 0.727)
quote: The exception is DE direction match, where perturbation mean scores 0.733 and PIE scores 0.727.

claim: Cross-dataset, seen perturbations: PIE Spearman effect size 0.627 vs 0.547
quote: its Spearman effect size is 0.627 versus 0.547

claim: Cross-dataset, unseen perturbations: PIE AUPRC 0.252 vs context mean 0.102
quote: with an AUPRC of 0.252 versus 0.102 and a Jaccard score of 0.123 versus 0.077

claim: PIE also has the highest AUPRC in both regimes when Jiang, X-Atlas/Orion or Arc VCC is held out
quote: PIE also achieves the highest AUPRC in both regimes when Jiang et al., X-Atlas/Orion or Arc VCC 2025 is held out

claim: Unseen contexts: Same-pert Evidence + Perturbation Knowledge Sources account for 0.169 of the 0.184 AUPRC gain
quote: Same-pert Evidence and Perturbation Knowledge Sources account for 0.169 of this 0.184 gain

claim: Unseen perturbations: small AUPRC gain of 0.045 spread across all five groups
quote: For unseen perturbations, the smaller AUPRC gain of 0.045 is distributed across all five groups.

claim: Unseen perturbations: Perturbation Knowledge Sources contribute 0.205 of the 0.207 Discrimination Score L1 gain
quote: Perturbation Knowledge Sources account for nearly the entire gain in Discrimination Score L1, contributing 0.205 of 0.207.

claim: Both unseen: Perturbation Knowledge Sources have negative mean AUPRC attribution but drive direction, LFC and discrimination gains
quote: Perturbation Knowledge Sources have a negative mean AUPRC attribution, but account for most of the improvement in DE direction match, Spearman LFC, and Discrimination Score L1.

claim: Unseen perturbations: DepMap contributes the most AUPRC among knowledge sources (0.013); ESM2 0.000
quote: Of this gain, DepMap contributes 0.013, STRING 0.008, and NCBI Gene Annotations 0.006; ESM2 contributes 0.000 and the Perturbation Description −0.002.

claim: The Perturbation Description has a negative AUPRC Shapley value in all three regimes
quote: The Perturbation Description has a negative AUPRC value in all three regimes.

claim: Chemical perturbations add L1000 transcriptional, PRISM viability and JUMP morphological profiles
quote: three measured activity profiles: transcriptional responses from L1000 (Subramanian et al., 2017), viability effects from PRISM (Corsello et al., 2020), and morphological effects from JUMP

claim: DE label = Wilcoxon rank-sum test with BH FDR < 0.05
quote: indicates whether a Wilcoxon rank-sum test yields a Benjamini–Hochberg FDR below 0.05

claim: Performance is weaker for perturbations with small effect sizes
quote: Performance was also weaker for perturbations with small effect sizes, where distinguishing biological signal from experimental variation is particularly challenging.

claim: Performance declined when contexts and perturbations were jointly unseen
quote: performance declined when contexts and perturbations were jointly unseen
